The denominator is $2-6\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $2+6\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $2+6\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-4}{2-6\text{i}} & =\frac{-4}{2-6\text{i}}\cdot \frac{2+6\text{i}}{2+6\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-8-24\text{i}}{4+12\text{i}-12\text{i}-36{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-8-24\text{i}}{4-36{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-8-24\text{i}}{4-(36)(-1)} \\  & =\frac{-8-24\text{i}}{4+36} \\  & =\frac{-8-24\text{i}}{40}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-8-24\text{i}}{40}=-\frac{8}{40}-\frac{24}{40}\text{i}=(-\frac{1}{5})+(-\frac{3}{5})\,\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
